purpose: Canonical conversational gateway and operational memory for autonomous agents scanning, triaging, implementing, and tracking all upstream OSS contributions.

agent_directive.canonicality_rule: This file is the primary and authoritative source of truth for the unified OSS PR-hunt and implementation workflow. All future agents, including GLM 5.3 Flash and later agents, must read it first and use its current schema, section structure, field names, and conventions as the canonical format.
agent_directive.before_action: Read this file before proposing, claiming, implementing, or submitting a new upstream OSS target, regardless of project domain.
agent_directive.after_action: Update this file after every meaningful outcome: new target, competing PR, maintainer feedback, review request, merge, closure, auto-close, rejection, or change in refile/duplicate eligibility.
agent_directive.update_rule: When operational state changes, update triage.json itself in its existing format. Preserve the current schema, section structure, field names, and conventions; update only affected records; keep dates and current state accurate; do not create parallel memory files or leave the canonical record stale.
hard_exclusions: Do not duplicate work already represented by an active or completed contribution unless upstream state has materially changed.
Do not refile targets marked do_not_refile=true unless new upstream information explicitly changes that decision.
Do not target issues with visible owner/claim, reserved maintainer work, or a competing PR covering the same semantics.
Do not submit work that repository policy or AI-assistance policy makes unsuitable.
Do not compete with a PR that appeared after the current scan; refresh upstream state immediately before acting.
Do not maintain separate domain-specific operational queues; all OSS work belongs in this unified ledger.
Do not treat historical ledger repositories as separate sources of truth; this repository is the canonical unified ledger.
agent_directive.freshness_rule: Triage memory is historical/operational context, not a substitute for a live GitHub check. Re-check issue, PR, assignees, comments, reviews, CI, mergeability, and competing work before action.
agent_directive.scan_output_rule: Dated scan files should record only what is new on their date; carryover rows verified unchanged do not need to be repeated.
agent_directive.implementation_rule: Prefer bounded, reproducible patches with regression tests where the repository has an applicable test suite; validate against the exact upstream default branch before claiming correctness.
agent_directive.unified_queue_rule: Rank all candidates together using the same eligibility, fit, scope, maintainer, freshness, and merge-potential criteria. Domain is informational only and must not by itself prioritize or exclude a target.

selection_criteria: Issue or behavior is reproducible or source-verifiable.
Target fits the contributor's practical stack.
Patch scope is bounded and locally testable.
No visible owner, reserved work, or competing pull request covers the same work.
Expected behavior is sufficiently clear to implement without speculative design.
Fix is not already present on current upstream main/default branch.
Work is legitimate upstream OSS work and is eligible for external contribution.
Work is not mainly churn, vague features, documentation trivia, or difficult to validate locally.
Target does not refile work previously auto-closed, rejected, or otherwise excluded in this ledger.
preflight_checklist: Refresh issue state, assignees, comments, and cross-referenced PRs via the core GitHub API.
Read the relevant triage records in this file, including prior attempts, competing PRs, maintainer feedback, and exclusion flags.
Re-read the target repository's contribution and AI-assistance policy.
Reproduce on the exact upstream default branch, not only the latest release.
Post a concise, human-reviewed claim/approach comment only where repository etiquette calls for it.
Keep the patch bounded and add a failing-first regression where tests exist.
Run the narrow test, formatter/linter/type checker, then the feasible package suite.
Link the issue with the repository's required keyword and disclose AI assistance where required.
Refresh competing-PR state immediately before submission; never knowingly compete with newer upstream work.
Use this unified ledger as the single queue and triage memory for all future target selection.

scan_mechanics.issue_discovery: Bulk issue discovery should use repository-native issue discovery and avoid high-volume search fan-out. Cross-check candidate issues through timeline events before implementation.
scan_mechanics.competing_pr_detection: Use per-issue timeline cross-referenced events and keyword search. A resolved reference must be confirmed as a live PR for the same repository/behavior before classifying it as a competitor.
scan_mechanics.raced_target_rule: If the issue timeline or keyword search reveals a competing open PR for the same issue or behavior, immediately classify the candidate as contested/raced, stop GO evaluation, and move on. Do not spend additional implementation, policy-analysis, or deep-testing effort unless the competing PR closes or upstream state materially changes.
scan_mechanics.persistent_raced_target_rule: Every raced/contested target must be recorded here with the issue, competing PR number(s), current status, verification date, and do_not_duplicate=true. Update the record when the competing PR closes, merges, or the issue changes materially.
